correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern hillside swale into the Hart Canyon drainage
correspondence.finding: The chosen short westward opening lies on the low slopes east of the Hart Canyon receiving hollow, and turns southwest into that open valley. The adjacent Nagel and Smith canyon labels do not name this selected opening. Ordinary swale-to-valley correspondence is supported by terrain; no permanent headwater stream or spring is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Weaver Creek and the Twin Oaks receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The mapped southern continuation of the Hart-side drainage is labeled Weaver Creek. It enters the Caliente Creek receiving corridor near the Twin Oaks setting. The stored generalized diagonal is not interpreted as an exact surveyed confluence or as extending Weaver over the downstream trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Twin Oaks–Loraine–Millersville corridor
correspondence.finding: Repeated Caliente Creek labels and the confined mapped valley establish the westward selected passage through Twin Oaks, Loraine and Millersville. Agua Caliente and Indian Creek enter separately from the south; their labels are not aliases of the selected composite.

correspondence.component_scope: Caliente Creek through the Fig Orchard and Caliente corridor
correspondence.finding: The channel continues west through the winding mountain valley, past Fig Orchard and the Caliente settlement. The selected route is the Caliente trunk; Tehachapi Creek joins from the southeast near Caliente.

correspondence.component_scope: Caliente–Ilmon–Bena lower confined valley
correspondence.finding: The mapped Caliente Creek valley turns northwest through Ilmon to Bena. Walker Basin Creek joins from the north near Bena. The route then reaches the open San Joaquin Valley fan; adjacent ridges do not form an intervening selected basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Bena fan, highway crossing and southward cultivated receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The stored part reaches the canyon mouth and runs south across the open cultivated fan toward eastern Arvin. The map labels a more westward managed Caliente alignment at Mountain View Road; it does not label the selected southern line as one channel. Topographic contours show the common descending fan, while the actually read Arvin planning prose establishes the surrounding plain as Caliente sheet-flow receiving ground. This is ordinary receiving-floor correspondence, not proof of current conveyance across every levee, road or field.

correspondence.component_scope: Spreading basins east of Arvin and southward/westward agricultural continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes the mapped pond/spreading-ground complex at Rockpile Road and Bear Mountain Boulevard, then continues across the lower cultivated fan to the south side of Arvin. The plan distinguishes Sycamore and Little Sycamore as eastern contributors. The mapping supports one common open receiving floor and local managed-water features; it does not establish one named natural stream or a specific active operating connection through these basins.

correspondence.component_scope: Cultivated plain south of Arvin toward the Kern Island Drain setting
correspondence.finding: The selected westward interval occupies the continuously descending cultivated plain, crosses mapped ditches and pond groups, and reaches the neighborhood of the Kern Island Drain. The regional and detailed originals show no mountain divide or separate intervening closed basin. This is generalized plain/fan transfer, with no assertion that the full rendered zigzag is a current ditch or that Kern Island Drain names the whole interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest continuation across the lower plain into Kern Lake Bed
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns southwest, crosses the highway setting, and reaches the flat mapped Kern Lake Bed. The independent historical project record explicitly places Caliente in the internal drainage contributing to this bed. The source supports a receiving setting, not exact present flood routes, a permanently wet lake or a newly inferred downstream outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected interior ending in the eastern Kern Lake Bed
correspondence.finding: The final stored part remains within the mapped flat agricultural/lake-bed interior west of the highway. The separate source and render terminal fields coincide in this same setting; the quantized geometry ending is retained separately. No extension to the Kern River, Buena Vista Lake or the sea is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastward opening east of Castro Alves, eastward upper corridor and receiving join near the Sapeaçu boundary
correspondence.finding: Castro Alves 2022 depicts the selected opening branch, northeastward bend and connected eastward river corridor. Its blue drainage and underlying photographic valley setting can be followed into the directly labelled Rio Jaguaripe near the eastern municipal edge. Conceição 2020 provides overlapping cartographic context. This is geographic correspondence, not an extension of the name to every headwater or an identification of the river’s ultimate spring.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward Jaguaripe through the Conceição do Almeida and Comércio/Alto Jaguaripe setting
correspondence.finding: The Conceição 2020 original depicts the connected river south from the Sapeaçu/Castro Alves edge, past the Comércio, Mirante, Gurgel and Alto Jaguaripe setting, into the Dom Macedo Costa side of the mapped corridor. Direct upstream Rio Jaguaripe labels and the continuous mapped drainage establish the receiving identity. Administrative lines are not used as substitutes for the river connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle river south and southeast beside Dom Macedo Costa, Barra do Jaguaripe and Tapera do Jaguaripe
correspondence.finding: The original Conceição sheet shows the ordinary receiving valley past the Dom Macedo Costa-side tributary joins, Barra do Jaguaripe and Tapera do Jaguaripe, with lower coverage overlapping the Jaguaripe 2010 sheet. The latter continues the course toward Muniz Ferreira. No reservoir, lake transfer, separate-basin crossing or current water-management operation is required for this mapped connected corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower inland river through Muniz Ferreira and Onha toward Nazaré
correspondence.finding: Jaguaripe 2010 directly labels Rio Jaguaripe on the winding river through the Muniz Ferreira/Onha setting and into Nazaré. The selected bends and joins are continuously depicted. The separately joining Rio Onha is a contextual tributary, not a whole-selection alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Nazaré widening, eastward reach, southward estuarine turn and Aratuípe joining setting
correspondence.finding: The original lower map depicts widening Rio Jaguaripe below Nazaré, its connected southward estuarine corridor, and the separately named Rio Aratuípe entering from the west near Aratuípe and Maragogipinho. The selected route stays in the receiving estuary rather than extending upstream along that tributary. Mangrove margins and estuarine branches are ordinary connected receiving terrain.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward estuarine course along the north side of Jaguaripe town
correspondence.finding: The sheet directly labels Rio Jaguaripe on the eastward main estuarine course along the town’s northern side. It separately labels Rio da Dona along the southern side, joining the same broad receiving water east of town. Original imagery confirms the town peninsula and the open, connected estuarine junction. Rio da Dona remains a separately named joining river, not an alias or an extra selected upstream reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Final rendered southward extension and the separately recorded source ending
correspondence.finding: The source ending lies in open estuarine water east of Jaguaripe town at the broad Jaguaripe–Dona joining setting. The rendered ending lies farther south in the connected vegetated mangrove/tidal-flat margin, west of the mapped lower Rio Caboclo. The map and actually read imagery establish a common estuarine receiving floor and adjoining mangrove plain without a separate-basin transfer. The final straight rendered extension is not claimed to be a mapped natural river channel, and the rendered point is not substituted for the source mouth. Neither endpoint is extended to the open Atlantic or through Canal da Barra. No precise bank, individual wet thread, instantaneous tide or present flow claim is required or made.

terminal_description.source_endpoint: Open receiving water east of Jaguaripe town at the Jaguaripe–Dona estuarine junction.
terminal_description.render_endpoint: Farther south in the same connected estuarine mangrove/tidal-flat margin, west of mapped lower Rio Caboclo. It is not the same point or a newly identified natural-river mouth.
terminal_description.scope_limit: The selected route is not extended to open Atlantic water or along Canal da Barra.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern hillside opening and long southward valley
correspondence.finding: The actual chosen opening is a small hollow entering the western side of a long north–south intermontane valley. The original upper image shows the continuous valley floor, tributary fans from both sides and the southward receiving corridor. The modeled first part follows this common floor rather than crossing the flanking ridges. No spring name, exact active thread or permanent surface flow is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Cultivated valley continuation and southeastern bend
correspondence.finding: The short intervening part and longer southern pieces remain within the same valley through a cultivated settlement/fan setting. At the southern end the floor turns southeast around the end of the eastern ridge. A continuous low passage and receiving wash/fan belt can be followed; no separate-basin jump is required by this correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward connecting valley and narrow foothill passage
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor bends east through a cultivated low passage between the ridge ends. Tributary fan aprons enter from the north and south. The connection is visible as one open valley floor around the hill noses, without claiming that every quantized segment is the exact dry channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast outlet fan, eastern plain and northward bend around a low hill
correspondence.finding: The selected part leaves the narrow western passage, follows the broad eastward receiving fan/plain across the road setting, and bends northeast around the north side of an isolated low ridge toward a cultivated patch. The original overview and enlarged lower pixels show a continuous interlinked fan/valley floor around that ridge, rather than a ridge crossing or transfer out of an isolated lake. The visible field layout and pale swales support geographic orientation only; exact present conveyance is unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward turn beside the eastern ridge and southeast receiving valley
correspondence.finding: The path turns south along the ridge-foot side of the cultivated patch, passes a more incised/dark vegetated drainage belt, and follows the open valley southeast around the next hill. Multiple local fan contributions enter the same corridor. The chosen route is not assumed to be a single named natural stream simply because the floor is connected.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward open plain and southeast cultivated fan belt
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues east across a broad open receiving surface and then southeast through the pale cultivated fan belt. The enlarged original shows continuous alluvial ground between the higher ridge margins and the open southern plain. Scene haze and agricultural alteration limit fine-channel interpretation but do not hide the enclosing passage or require a separate-basin connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern fan margin and common lower alluvial floor
correspondence.finding: The route leaves the cultivated upper fan, passes around the southern foot of a broad low hill and joins the wider eastern alluvial receiving floor. Northern branching drainage and southern pale wash surfaces occupy this shared low setting. The generalized horizontal modeled intervals are treated as receiving-floor passages, not a proven current channel or evidence of perennial water.

correspondence.component_scope: Short eastern terminal segment at the margin of the alluvial drainage belt
correspondence.finding: The final part bends northeast and then east into the same alluvial interior, beside the broad branching drainage belt arriving from the north. The stored ending is not in a clearly bounded named lake and is not extended to another river or coast. Source and render terminal fields coincide but remain separately recorded; the stored quantized endpoint is retained separately. No underground continuation, current flow direction or channel-name boundary is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern mountain feeder and southwest descent.
correspondence.finding: The upper original exposes the selected opening in a small mountain drainage hollow. Its incised, locally greener trough descends west and southwest through the hills and opens into a broader pale alluvial receiving valley. Side hollows enter the same trough. Nearby small clouds do not conceal the necessary connection. This is a chosen tributary opening, not the head of the entire Pisco river system. No precise hydronym is assigned to the first position.

correspondence.component_scope: Broadening tributary valley and multiple receiving joins.
correspondence.finding: The short second part enters the broad receiving floor from the northeast. The third continues southwest where a substantial northern side valley joins. The imagery shows an uninterrupted alluvial valley and tributary-fan surfaces; a blue or presently wet line is unnecessary to identify the ordinary receiving connection. No divide, lake crossing or isolated basin intervenes. The report independently describes seasonal Veladero drainage as a Pisco contributor, but its prose does not fix a name boundary on each upper fork.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward tributary canyon and transfer into the receiving Pisco valley.
correspondence.finding: Parts4 and5 descend the same confined valley toward the wider cultivated river corridor. At the end of part5 and beginning of part6, the northern tributary opens directly into that receiving valley; the selection then turns southwest with the main corridor. The ordinary confluence is visually exposed. This matches the report’s separate seasonal Veladero contributor and Pisco receiving-system hierarchy. Veladero remains a bounded tributary attribution; its name is not extended uniformly over every selected headward fork.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest Pisco valley and opening toward the lower agricultural valley.
correspondence.finding: The upper detail and overview show the continuous winding main valley southwest from the receiving join. Tributary mouths, gravel channel belts and patches of cultivation remain within one connected trough. Parts7–12 pass successive valley bends and gradually wider cultivated floors. Source prose places the Pisco main river through the middle receiving basin and into the lower valley at Letrayoc; station names provide context rather than exact point assignments to stored vertices. No reservoir or separate managed transfer is needed to explain these parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad lower valley, westward bend and approach to the coastal plain.
correspondence.finding: The overview and lower original expose the westward and northwestward valley continuation through the full agricultural receiving floor. Wide gravel channels, irrigated fields, roads and lateral fans remain in the same connected valley. Small clouds near the short fourteenth part obscure local surface detail, while the adjacent broad floor, entering and leaving corridor and wider continuity remain clear. They do not leave a material through-link unresolved. The generalized selection need not follow every present channel bend.

correspondence.component_scope: Final coastal receiving plain, mouth setting and Pacific shore.
correspondence.finding: The final part crosses the wide lower river belt and its cultivated coastal receiving floor north of the main Pisco urban area. The lower original shows the channel belt reaching the coastal outlet zone, the beach-margin drainage and the adjoining Pacific. The supplied nearly straight segment is retained as an ordinary receiving-floor correspondence rather than interpreted as a surveyed current channel. No enclosed terminal lake or missing coastal transfer appears.

correspondence.component_scope: Original-source sea terminal, evaluated separately.
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint lies in nearshore Pacific water, seaward and slightly northwest of the rendered endpoint. It represents the common marine receiving setting next to the lower Pisco outlet. It is preserved without being moved onto a visible beach edge or current channel mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Rendered coastal terminal, evaluated separately.
correspondence.finding: The distinct rendered endpoint lies landward and southeast of the source endpoint at the beach-margin outlet setting, where the lower river belt meets the coastal drainage strip. Its supplied position and sea-terminal classification are preserved. The imagery supports the Pacific receiving setting, not a claim that this exact point is presently open water or an active tidal outlet.
